overall: Atlanta is off to a surprisingly slow and irregular start on June 16th. Despite it being nearly 10 AM, the current temperature of 68.0°F sits well below the running max of 73.4°F — which was set as far back as 7:00 AM and has not budged since, suggesting a morning cooling episode (possibly cloud cover, a brief outflow boundary, or light precipitation) suppressed temperatures after an early peak. The high dewpoint of 62.6°F and light winds indicate a humid, marginally unstable airmass, and the current warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr suggests temperatures are now recovering.
forecast_obs_notes: The three NWP models show reasonable clustering in the 76.5–79.2°F range (HRRR=76.5, ECMWF=77.0, NBM=79.2), but observed temperatures are running meaningfully below all of them as of 09:50 ET, implying the models did not capture the morning setback. The ensemble signals are starkly split — the even model points to 74–75°F while the odd model targets 81–82°F, both at identical 29% Tier 1 confidence — reflecting genuine uncertainty about whether the morning suppression will persist or relax fully into the afternoon.
max_temp_prediction: Projecting from 68.0°F at 09:50 ET at a gradually decelerating +1.8°F/hr warming rate, temperatures could reach the upper 70s by mid-afternoon if no further convective or frontal interference occurs, broadly consistent with the ECMWF/HRRR guidance near 77°F. However, the stubborn morning cool-down and the high-confidence lower ensemble signal (74–75°F) introduce meaningful downside risk — if cloud cover or outflow persists into the afternoon, the max may struggle to clear 76°F. Weighing the NWP model consensus against the morning underperformance, the best estimate is approximately 77.0°F with moderate confidence and a slight lean toward the cooler side of model guidance.
